html:
Florida (Spain) is the map's name for Spanish Florida in 1715, after its mission system had been destroyed. For the colony's earlier years see Spanish Florida.

By 1715 raids from English Carolina had wiped out most of the missions, and Spain held little more than St. Augustine and Pensacola, founded in 1698. That year the Yamasee War in Carolina sent the Yamasee and other peoples south as Spanish allies. Spain offered freedom to enslaved people who escaped from the English colonies, and in 1738 built Fort Mose for them, the first legal free Black town in North America.

Spain gave Florida to Britain in 1763, got it back in 1783, and sold it to the United States by the Adams Onís Treaty, which took effect in 1821. In the meantime Creek migrants and escaped slaves had formed the Seminole.
